cases.translation: The day was once again clear and warm.
cases.explain: "День" is the subject of "был" (was), so it stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Раскольников сел на складенные у ___ бревна и стал глядеть на реку.
cases.translation: Raskolnikov sat on the logs stacked by the shed and began looking at the river.
cases.explain: "Сарая" is genitive because of the preposition "у" (by the shed).

cases.sentence: Платье его было тепло и приспособлено к его ___ жизни.
cases.translation: His clothing was warm and suited to his way of life.
cases.explain: "Образу" is dative because of the preposition "к" (suited to his way of life).

cases.sentence: Раскольников сел на бревна и стал глядеть на широкую и пустынную ___.
cases.translation: Raskolnikov sat on the logs and began looking at the wide, empty river.
cases.explain: "Реку" is accusative as the object of "глядеть на" (looking at the river).

cases.sentence: На второй неделе великого поста пришла ему очередь говеть вместе с своей ___.
cases.translation: In the second week of Lent it was his turn to fast and pray together with his barracks.
cases.explain: "Казармой" is instrumental because of the preposition "с" (together with his barracks).

cases.sentence: Он пролежал в ___ весь конец поста и Святую.
cases.translation: He lay in the hospital through the rest of Lent and Easter week.
cases.explain: "Больнице" is prepositional because of the preposition "в" (in the hospital).

reading.ru: Он был болен уже давно; но не ужасы каторжной жизни, не работы, не пища, не бритая голова, не лоскутное платье сломили его
reading.question: What does the narrator say did NOT break Raskolnikov's spirit in prison?
options: The horrors of convict life, the labor, the food, his shaved head, his ragged clothes
His fellow convicts' hatred of him
reading.correct: The horrors of convict life, the labor, the food, his shaved head, his ragged clothes
reading.explain: The text lists these hardships explicitly as things that did not break him.

reading.ru: Но не бритой головы и кандалов он стыдился: его гордость сильно была уязвлена; он и заболел от уязвленной гордости.
reading.question: What was the true cause of Raskolnikov's illness, according to the text?
reading.correct: His wounded pride
reading.explain: It was not his shaved head or chains that shamed him, but his deeply wounded pride, which is what actually made him ill.

reading.ru: Зачем ему жить? Что иметь в виду? К чему стремиться?
reading.question: What existential questions does Raskolnikov ask himself about his future?
options: Why live, what to aim for, what to strive toward
Whether he will ever see his mother again
How long his sentence will last
reading.correct: Why live, what to aim for, what to strive toward
reading.explain: He asks himself why he should live, what he should have in view, and what he should strive for.

reading.ru: Но он не раскаивался в своем преступлении.
reading.question: Does Raskolnikov feel repentance for his crime at this point?
reading.correct: No, he does not repent
reading.explain: The text states plainly that he did not repent of his crime.

reading.ru: Чем, чем, — думал он, — моя мысль была глупее других мыслей и теорий, роящихся и сталкивающихся одна с другой на свете, с тех пор как этот свет стоит?
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov argue in his own defense, in his thoughts?
options: That his idea was no more foolish than countless other theories in the world
That his idea was inspired by Sonya
That his idea came from reading Napoleon's biography
That his idea was purely accidental
reading.correct: That his idea was no more foolish than countless other theories in the world
reading.explain: He asks himself how his thought could be any more foolish than the countless other ideas and theories that have clashed in the world since it began.

reading.ru: Совесть моя спокойна.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov claim about his conscience?
options: That he has no conscience at all
reading.correct: That it is at peace
reading.explain: He states directly, "My conscience is at peace."

reading.ru: Вот в чем одном признавал он свое преступление: только в том, что не вынес его и сделал явку с повинною.
reading.question: In what does Raskolnikov say his true "crime" consisted?
options: In failing to endure his secret and confessing
reading.correct: In failing to endure his secret and confessing
reading.explain: He admits his only real fault was that he could not bear the weight of his secret and turned himself in.

reading.ru: Он смотрел на каторжных товарищей своих и удивлялся: как тоже все они любили жизнь, как они дорожили ею!
reading.question: What surprises Raskolnikov about his fellow convicts?
options: How much they all loved and valued life
How little they cared about survival
How kind they were to him
reading.correct: How much they all loved and valued life
reading.explain: He is struck by how much his fellow convicts loved life and how dearly they valued it.

reading.ru: Казалось, он и они были разных наций.
reading.question: How did Raskolnikov feel he differed from the other convicts? (choose closest paraphrase)
options: As if he and they belonged to entirely different peoples
As if he alone spoke a foreign language
As if he alone had committed a crime
As if he alone was innocent
reading.correct: As if he and they belonged to entirely different peoples
reading.explain: It seemed to him that he and the other convicts were like people of different nations entirely.

reading.ru: Ты барин! — говорили ему. — Тебе ли было с топором ходить; не барское вовсе дело.
reading.question: What do the other convicts say to mock Raskolnikov?
options: That as a gentleman, wielding an axe was not his kind of business
That he was too weak to survive prison
That he should have used poison instead
reading.correct: That as a gentleman, wielding an axe was not his kind of business
reading.explain: They taunt him, saying he is a gentleman and that going about with an axe was not a gentleman's business.

reading.ru: На второй неделе великого поста пришла ему очередь говеть вместе с своей казармой.
reading.question: What religious obligation comes up for Raskolnikov during Lent?
options: His turn to fast and pray with his barracks
His turn to confess to a priest alone
His turn to lead a service
reading.correct: His turn to fast and pray with his barracks
reading.explain: In the second week of Lent it was his turn to observe fasting and prayer together with his barracks.

reading.ru: Он никогда не говорил с ними о боге и о вере, но они хотели убить его как безбожника; он молчал и не возражал им.
reading.question: How does Raskolnikov respond when accused of being a godless man?
options: He stays silent and does not argue
He argues fiercely in his defense
reading.correct: He stays silent and does not argue
reading.explain: Though he never discussed God or faith with them, they wanted to kill him as a godless man; he remained silent and did not object.

reading.ru: Неразрешим был для него еще один вопрос: почему все они так полюбили Соню?
reading.question: What unsolved question puzzles Raskolnikov about the other convicts?
options: Why they all came to love Sonya
Why they hated him so much
reading.correct: Why they all came to love Sonya
reading.explain: He could not understand why all the convicts had come to love Sonya so much.

reading.ru: Ему грезилось в болезни, будто весь мир осужден в жертву какой-то страшной, неслыханной и невиданной моровой язве, идущей из глубины Азии на Европу.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov dream about while feverish in the hospital?
options: That the whole world was doomed by a terrible plague spreading from Asia to Europe
That he was pardoned and freed
reading.correct: That the whole world was doomed by a terrible plague spreading from Asia to Europe
reading.explain: In his illness he dreamed that the entire world was condemned to a terrible, unprecedented plague spreading from Asia into Europe.

reading.ru: Раскольникова мучило то, что этот бессмысленный бред так грустно и так мучительно отзывается в его воспоминаниях, что так долго не проходит впечатление этих горячешных грез.
reading.question: What continues to torment Raskolnikov after recovering?
options: That the impression of his feverish dreams lingers painfully in his memory
That his mother has stopped writing
That his sentence has been extended
reading.correct: That the impression of his feverish dreams lingers painfully in his memory
reading.explain: He is tormented that the memory of this senseless, feverish delirium stays with him so sadly and painfully for so long.

reading.ru: Он был очень беспокоен, посылал о ней справляться.
reading.question: How does Raskolnikov react when he learns Sonya has fallen ill?
options: He becomes very anxious and sends to inquire about her
He asks to be transferred to see her
He refuses to think about it
reading.correct: He becomes very anxious and sends to inquire about her
reading.explain: He grew very anxious and sent people to inquire about her condition.

reading.ru: Раскольников вышел из сарая на самый берег, сел на складенные у сарая бревна и стал глядеть на широкую и пустынную реку.
reading.question: Where does Raskolnikov sit and look out at the river?
options: On logs stacked by the shed, on the riverbank
On a bench inside the prison yard
On a boat crossing the river
reading.correct: On logs stacked by the shed, on the riverbank
reading.explain: He came out of the shed onto the riverbank and sat on logs stacked there, gazing at the wide, empty river.

reading.ru: Вдруг подле него очутилась Соня.
reading.question: Who suddenly appears beside Raskolnikov by the river?
reading.correct: Sonya
reading.explain: Suddenly Sonya appeared at his side, having approached almost silently.

reading.ru: Но теперь их руки не разнимались; он мельком и быстро взглянул на нее, ничего не выговорил и опустил свои глаза в землю.
reading.question: What is different about Raskolnikov and Sonya's hands in this scene, compared to before?
options: Their hands do not separate this time
He refuses to hold her hand
reading.correct: Their hands do not separate this time
reading.explain: Unlike before, this time their hands did not part; he glanced at her quickly and lowered his eyes.

reading.ru: Он плакал и обнимал ее колени.
reading.question: How does Raskolnikov express his feelings in this pivotal moment?
options: He weeps and embraces her knees
reading.correct: He weeps and embraces her knees
reading.explain: Something suddenly seized him and threw him at her feet; he wept and embraced her knees.

reading.ru: Их воскресила любовь, сердце одного заключало бесконечные источники жизни для сердца другого.
reading.question: What is said to have brought Raskolnikov and Sonya to a new life?
options: Love resurrected them, each heart a source of life for the other
reading.correct: Love resurrected them, each heart a source of life for the other
reading.explain: The text says love had resurrected them, with each heart holding endless springs of life for the other.

reading.ru: Им оставалось еще семь лет; а до тех пор столько нестерпимой муки и столько бесконечного счастия!
reading.question: How many years does the couple still have left of the sentence?
reading.correct: Seven years
reading.explain: The text notes they still had seven years ahead of them, filled with both unbearable suffering and boundless happiness.

reading.ru: Да и что такое эти все, все муки прошлого!
reading.question: How does Raskolnikov now regard the sufferings of his past, in this moment of renewal?
options: As insignificant compared to his new feelings
As something Sonya must still pay for
reading.correct: As insignificant compared to his new feelings
reading.explain: In this moment he dismisses all his past suffering as nothing compared to what he now feels.

reading.ru: Он взял его машинально.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov do with the Gospel found under his pillow?
options: He picks it up mechanically, without thinking
He gives it back to Sonya
reading.correct: He picks it up mechanically, without thinking
reading.explain: He picked up the Gospel from under his pillow mechanically, without particular thought.

reading.ru: Но тут уж начинается новая история, история постепенного обновления человека, история постепенного перерождения его, постепенного перехода из одного мира в другой, знакомства с новою, доселе совершенно неведомою действительностью.
reading.question: How does the novel's narrator describe what lies ahead for Raskolnikov?
options: A new story of gradual renewal and rebirth into an unknown reality
A story that will never be told
A repetition of his past mistakes
An immediate return to his old life
reading.correct: A new story of gradual renewal and rebirth into an unknown reality
reading.explain: The narrator closes by saying a new story begins here — one of gradual renewal, rebirth, and transition into a completely unknown new reality.
